title: Postgres update of polymorphic object generates invalid SQL with synchronize_session='fetch'

labels.name: inheritance
labels.description: issues to do wtih ORM inheritance, a particularly tricky area

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
originally at #8332.    after looking at what we currently support, this is a bug.

### Describe the bug

When updating an object with `polymorphic_identity` and using `synchronize_session="fetch"`, SQLAlchemy's PostgreSQL dialect generates invalid SQL. Specifically, it tries to fetch columns from the base table without including it in a `FROM` clause.

We're migrating an app from 1.3 to 1.4 and have hit this in a number of places. Most cases can be replaced with the `evaluate` method, so it hasn't been a blocker.

### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy.orm import as_declarative, relationship, Session
from sqlalchemy.engine import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.sql.schema import Column, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.sql.sqltypes import Integer, String

@as_declarative()
class Base:
    pass


class Resource(Base):
    __tablename__ = "Resource"
    resource_id = Column("resource_id", Integer, primary_key=True)
    resource_type = Column("resource_type", String)

    __mapper_args__ = dict(polymorphic_on=resource_type, polymorphic_identity=__tablename__)


class Thing(Resource):
    __tablename__ = "Thing"
    __mapper_args__ = dict(polymorphic_identity=__tablename__)

    thing_id = Column("thing_id", ForeignKey(Resource.resource_id), primary_key=True)
    thing_name = Column(String)


engine = create_engine('postgresql:///test', echo=True)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

session = Session(engine)

thing1 = Thing(thing_name="foo")
thing2 = Thing(thing_name="bar")

session.add_all([thing1, thing2])
session.commit()

# This succeeds
session.query(Thing).filter(Thing.thing_name == "foo").update(dict(thing_name="baz"), synchronize_session="evaluate")

# But this fails with
## sqlalchemy.exc.ProgrammingError: (psycopg2.errors.UndefinedTable) missing FROM-clause entry for table "Resource"
## LINE 1: ...='baz' WHERE "Thing".thing_name = 'foo' RETURNING "Resource"...
session.query(Thing).filter(Thing.thing_name == "baz").update(dict(thing_name="quix"), synchronize_session="fetch")
```

[SQL: UPDATE "Thing" SET thing_name=%(thing_name)s WHERE "Thing".thing_name = %(thing_name_1)s RETURNING "Resource".resource_id]

### Versions

- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Python: 3.9.10
- SQLAlchemy: 1.4.39
- Database: Postgresql 12.8
- DBAPI (eg: psycopg, cx_oracle, mysqlclient): psycopg2 2.9.3
